# vendor/: the pinned copy of public Rovara Code

Convergence plan W0-1 (owner decision 72, O1): Cloud carries a read-only copy of public Rovara Code at one exact sha, so Cloud code can import Code's
packages while Cloud still builds as one repository. Packages published from Code's mainline come later (wave 4). Nothing in Cloud's own code imports
this yet except `tests/contract/vendor-rovara-code-smoke.test.ts`.

## What is here

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `rovara-code/` | The files of public `PrepLabsAI/Rovara` at the sha in `rovara-code/PIN`, byte for byte: `packages/{broker,contracts,gateway,local-adapters,model-runtime,verifier,worker}`, `tsconfig.base.json`, the licence files and `docs/ports.md`. `PIN` is the only file that is not Code's. **Never edit anything else in it.** |
| `rovara-code-shims/<pkg>/` | Generated npm workspace packages named `@rovara-code/<pkg>`. Each re-exports Code's `@agentx/<pkg>` (every subpath of its `exports` map; for the broker also `core/<module>` and `ports`). Checked in, regenerated by the update script. |
| `node_modules/@agentx/<pkg>` | Committed relative symlinks to `rovara-code/packages/<pkg>` (the one `.gitignore` exception for `node_modules`), plus `playwright-core`, a link to the 1.63.0 copy Code's verifier pins. |

## Why these names

Code and Cloud both publish `@agentx/*`, and npm refuses two workspaces with one name. So the pristine tree is **not** an npm workspace (its
`package.json` files keep their names, and `npm ci` never sees them). Instead:

- Cloud code imports `@rovara-code/<pkg>` (the generated shims, which are workspaces, so `npm ci` links them under `node_modules/@rovara-code/`).
- Inside `rovara-code/`, Code's own imports of `@agentx/contracts` and the like must reach Code's packages, not Cloud's. Node, TypeScript, Vite and esbuild all
  resolve a bare name by walking up from the importing file, so `vendor/node_modules/@agentx/*` (found before the repository's `node_modules`) does it with no
  loader hook, no `paths` mapping and no edit to a vendored file. A path mapping could not: TypeScript has one `paths` table per program.
- Wave 0 lane W0-3 renames Cloud's contracts to `@agentx/cloud-contracts`. When Code's contracts take the name `@agentx/contracts` in Cloud, the shim layer is
  the one place to change.

Code's third-party dependencies resolve to Cloud's installed packages (same lockfile family). `verify-rovara-code.ts` fails if any of them resolves to a version other
than the one Code declares; the one existing difference (`playwright-core`) is the link in `THIRD_PARTY_LINKS`.

## Build, lint, tests, coverage

- The root `tsconfig.json` references Code's own project files (`vendor/rovara-code/packages/*`), so `tsc -b` builds Code's `dist/` here (git-ignored) with Code's
  own compiler options before Cloud's packages that import it. A cold build adds about a minute.
- `eslint.config.js` ignores `vendor/rovara-code/**` and `vendor/rovara-code-shims/**`; `tsconfig.lint.json` and the lint programs do not list `vendor/`; the
  typecheck baseline therefore never sees it. Vitest's include globs (`tests/**`, `packages/**`) do not match it, and coverage is off. Code's own tests are not copied.
- Cloud's `.dockerignore` excludes `node_modules/`, so a Docker build that needs Code must copy `vendor/node_modules` explicitly (nothing does yet).

## Refresh the pin

```sh
node scripts/vendor/update-rovara-code.ts            # head of public code/next (or: <40-character sha> | <branch>)
npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts      # only if the set of shims changed
npx tsc -b && git add -A vendor package-lock.json
```

The script fetches that one sha (no history), runs `git archive` for the include list, checks the extracted files against `git ls-tree` of the sha, replaces
`rovara-code/`, rewrites `PIN` (sha, include list, file count, manifest hash) and regenerates the shims and links. Change what is copied in `INCLUDE`
(`scripts/vendor/rovara-code-vendor.ts`).

## Check it

```sh
node scripts/vendor/verify-rovara-code.ts            # offline: files hash to PIN's manifest; shims, links and dependency versions are current
node scripts/vendor/verify-rovara-code.ts --remote   # also fetches the pinned sha's tree from the public repo and compares file by file (CI's vendor step)
```

`tests/contract/vendor-rovara-code.test.ts` runs the offline check on every test run (and the remote one when `ROVARA_VENDOR_VERIFY_REMOTE=1`).

## Rules

- Upstream first (plan 3.1): change Code's files in Code, through its lane, controller and port-guard, then update the pin. A Cloud hotfix that cannot wait may
  not edit the vendored copy either: the PIN check fails. It needs a pin to a Code sha that has the fix.
- Never import `vendor/rovara-code/...` by path from Cloud code; import `@rovara-code/<pkg>`.
